display.title: The Mitteler Rebbe's Cossacks: Simcha Breaks a Decree (Adar)
display.summary_short: For the month of Adar, a lesson on doubling our simcha every day, and the story of the Mitteler Rebbe, who called for music and dancing to cancel a Heavenly decree against his son.
display.summary_long: Each Yom Tov gives strength for the whole year, and Adar is the month for gathering simcha. The storyteller explains the Rebbe's teaching that 'marbin b'simcha' means doubling our joy every day, with a riddle: a penny doubled daily for a month beats a gift of a million dollars. A short story follows of the young Rebbe Maharash, a playful boy who behaved perfectly when his father, the Tzemach Tzedek, came to check on him. Simcha, he explains, is the strongest way to cancel a harsh decree: the Zohar teaches that Hashem reflects a joyful face with blessing, and the Alter Rebbe smiled at his interrogators' hardest question. Then the main story: the Mitteler Rebbe kept a choir, musicians and a troupe of Chassidim who dressed up as Cossacks and rode horses in circles. One ordinary weekday he suddenly called for a great celebration and clapped along from his window. When his son Reb Nochum fell from his horse, the Rebbe clapped even harder. Afterwards he explained that he had seen a decree in Heaven against his son, and only simcha could break it; Reb Nochum's injury healed completely.
display.lesson: Simcha opens the channel for Hashem's blessings and can break even a harsh decree; in Adar, add more joy every day and make others happy too.
